Summarize the following in exactly 3 bullet points.

Remote work has reshaped how software teams operate. Surveys show most engineers now work in hybrid arrangements, splitting time between home and the office. Supporters argue that fewer commutes improve focus and widen the hiring pool, letting companies recruit talent from anywhere. Critics counter that spontaneous collaboration suffers, that junior engineers learn more slowly without proximity to mentors, and that company culture becomes harder to sustain. Several large firms have recently required staff to return to offices three days a week, citing productivity and onboarding concerns, while others doubled down on fully remote models and report lower attrition. Research is mixed: some studies find output unchanged or higher for individual tasks, while others note reduced innovation in cross-team work. Managers increasingly rely on written communication, documented decisions and asynchronous reviews to keep distributed teams aligned. Real estate costs have fallen for companies that downsized offices, but travel budgets for periodic in-person gatherings have risen. The emerging consensus is that the best arrangement depends on team maturity, the type of work, and how deliberately leaders design communication norms.
